passage:
Monday: Manoj built a block tower alone in the corner while Papa was on the phone. He stacked fast and crooked, and knocked it over with a laugh after five blocks.
Wednesday: Siddharth, his papa, sat on the floor beside him after dinner, just watching. Manoj slowed down. He turned each block so the edges matched, tongue between his teeth. Twelve blocks. "Papa, look! Look how tall!"
Saturday: Manoj dragged Papa by the hand to the play mat. "Sit here. Watch me." He built even slower this time, checking each block, and at the end he stood beside the tower with his arms out, like it was a trophy.

qa.q: How many blocks did Manoj stack on Wednesday?
qa.a: Twelve blocks.

qa.q: Why did Manoj slow down and match the edges on Wednesday?
qa.a: With Papa sitting beside him watching, he wanted to make something he could proudly show, so the tower felt worth the care.

qa.q: What choice by Siddharth made the difference, and what could he keep doing?
qa.a: He simply sat nearby and watched without taking over; making a little time to sit with Manoj during play can keep that care going.

qa.q: How might Siddharth feel when Manoj drags him to the mat on Saturday?
qa.a: He is likely touched and happy, seeing how much his watching matters to his son 😊.

grounding: Across a week, a small boy builds more carefully and proudly when his father sits and watches.

subtype: Working harder when someone is watching [Actor]
passage: The power had gone out, and the flat was lit by one candle on the floor. Wasim had a heap of paper cups. At first he stacked them quickly while his mother, Devika, searched for the torch in the kitchen. The cups tumbled. Then Devika came and sat on the floor with the torch, just watching. Wasim went quiet. He set each cup carefully, rim to rim, holding his breath. The shadow of the tower grew tall on the wall. "Mummy, see? See my tower's shadow!" He stepped back, eyes shining, and wouldn't let anyone touch it until the lights came back.

qa.q: What did Wasim build his tower from?
qa.a: From a heap of paper cups, set carefully rim to rim.

qa.q: What made Wasim go quiet and build carefully?
qa.a: His mother sitting beside him with the torch made him feel seen, so he wanted the tower to be good enough to show her.

qa.q: What small choice did Devika make that helped?
qa.a: She stopped searching and came to sit on the floor and watch, which gave Wasim the attention that fed his effort.

qa.q: What might Devika have felt seeing the tower's shadow on the wall?
qa.a: Devika may have felt warm and amused, sharing her son's pride in the dark room lit by one candle.

grounding: During a power cut, a small boy builds with new care once his mother sits and watches, then shows it proudly.

passage: In their Delhi flat, Gargi's mother, Neelam, finally shut her laptop at six and sat on the sofa with her tea. On the floor, Gargi had been building with wooden blocks all afternoon, half-hearted towers that fell over. Now she glanced up at her mother, then back at the blocks. She began again. This time she picked the big blocks for the bottom, pressed each one down with both hands, and put the little red triangle right on top. "Mumma! Look! It's a temple!" She stood beside it and wouldn't sit down until Neelam had come over and looked at it from every side.

qa.q: What did Gargi put right on top of the tower?
qa.a: The little red triangle.

qa.q: Why did Gargi glance up at her mother before starting again?
qa.a: She seemed to notice her mother was finally free and watching, which made her want to build something worth showing.

qa.q: What small habit could Neelam keep that helps Gargi's play?
qa.a: Taking a few minutes to sit nearby and watch, without directing, gives Gargi the attention that makes her try harder.

qa.q: How might Neelam feel being asked to look at the temple from every side?
qa.a: Neelam may feel tired but touched, realising how much simply being there mattered to Gargi.

grounding: A small girl builds with more care once her mother sits nearby, and shows the tower proudly.

passage:
'Ammi, sit here. No, HERE. Close.'
Sabina put down her phone and sat on the rug. 'Okay. I'm here.'
Karthik picked up a block, looked at her, and placed it very slowly. Then another. Tongue out.
'Wah. That's straight,' Sabina said.
'Watch this one. It's the hard one.' The little triangle went on top. It wobbled. Karthik held his breath. It stayed.
'Ammi! Look! LOOK! It's taller than Teddy!'
'It is. You built it so carefully.'
'I'm going to make a bigger one. You stay, okay? Don't go to the phone.'
'I'll stay.'

qa.q: What did Karthik put on top of the tower?
qa.a: The little triangle.

qa.q: Why did Karthik want Ammi to sit close and stay off the phone?
qa.a: Having her watch made him feel seen and proud; he wanted her attention while he worked carefully.

qa.q: What choice did Sabina make that helped Karthik's effort?
qa.a: She put down her phone, sat close and noticed specific things, like how straight and careful his building was; her attention fed his care and his wish to build more.

qa.q: What would change if Sabina had stayed on the phone?
qa.a: Karthik might have built faster and less carefully, or given up, and missed the pride of showing someone a tower 'taller than Teddy'.

grounding: A young child builds his tower with more care when his mother sits close, and proudly shows it to her.

subtype: Working harder when someone is watching [Actor]
passage:
Nursery note, parents' morning, Thursday. Urmila.
Sumit (4) usually builds block towers fast and knocks them down, laughing. Today his father sat on the small chair beside him for twenty minutes.
Sumit's building changed. He lined up every block with a finger before letting go, glancing at his father's face. When one wobbled, he fixed it instead of crashing it.
At the end he tugged his father's sleeve: 'Papa, it's a lighthouse. I did the window myself.'
After his father left, Sumit guarded the lighthouse till home time.

qa.q: What did Sumit say he had built?
qa.a: A lighthouse, with a window he did himself.

qa.q: Why did Sumit keep glancing at his father's face?
qa.a: He wanted his father to see what he was doing; being watched made him proud and careful.

qa.q: What did the parents' morning show about how to support Sumit's effort?
qa.a: That even twenty minutes of a parent sitting close changes how carefully Sumit works; being seen by someone he loves feeds his effort.

qa.q: How might Sumit's father feel when his son tugs his sleeve to show the lighthouse?
qa.a: He probably feels touched and proud, seeing how much his presence meant and how carefully Sumit built for him.

grounding: A nursery teacher notes a young child who builds much more carefully when his father sits beside him and proudly shows the result.
